target_offset_note:
DEFAULT [0, 0, +0.015]. Operator-verified on the floor-2 HALL CALL button, 2026-09-07, under tip aiming: it landed dead centre. Nothing else has been validated against two unrelated targets, so nothing else belongs here.

WHAT THIS REPLACED, AND WHY. It was [0.003, -0.020, 0.040] -- 40 mm of it straight UP -- tuned while approach_target.py aimed the hand-eye CALIBRATION MARKER at the target. The marker sits 25 mm above and 268 mm behind the fingertip at press orientation, so aiming it put the tip about 25 mm low and a quarter of a metre through the wall; the 40 mm cancelled part of that and did nothing about the rest. On a 120 mm ADA plate that was enough to look like a calibration. approach_target.py now aims the FINGERTIP (--tool-tip-mm, default 172), which made the 40 mm pure error -- and it is measurable: the hall call button grounds at 1.069 m off the floor against the 1.067 m ADA centreline this building is built to, from gdino plus depth alone. The old value is kept as target_offset_profiles.marker_aim_legacy for reading old runs; do NOT press with it.

PROFILES ARE FOR ONE TARGET EACH. lift_car_select [0, -0.023, 0.015] was walked out by the operator on the IN-CAR floor button on 2026-09-07 and is correct for that 25 mm button at waypoint f2_car_panel. It is NOT the rig's calibration and must never become the default again.

THE Y SIGN IS THE TRAP. +y in link_base is the ROBOT's left, which is the OPERATOR's right when standing in front of it. Tuning went 0 -> +10 -> +20 mm with no improvement before the inversion was spotted, then swung to -35 and settled at -23. Read the sign off the robot, not off yourself.

The hand-eye solve itself is untouched and still good: 2.96 mm RMS, worst 8.2 mm, 10 pairs, 63.8 deg rotation spread, flange-relative, tcp_offset zero.
